lede: A report often needs several counts side by side: mobile and desktop, purchases and sign-ups, days over and under budget. Putting a condition inside the aggregate gives them in one pass, and `pivot` turns the values of a column into columns of their own.
objectives: Count and sum only the rows that match a condition with `F.when` inside an aggregate
Explain why filtering first loses groups that a conditional aggregate keeps
Turn the values of a column into columns with `groupBy(...).pivot(...)`
List the pivot values yourself so the columns are fixed, and predict where a pivot gives NULL

blocks.md:
The tables come from an advertising platform. `impressions` has one row per ad shown, with the campaign and the `device` it was shown on; `conversions` one row per purchase, sign-up or lead; `budgets` one row per campaign per day. Each is loaded as a DataFrame with its own name, and `F` is `pyspark.sql.functions`.

An aggregate works on whatever column you give it, including one built by `F.when`. `F.when(F.col("device") == "mobile", 1).otherwise(0)` is 1 on mobile rows and 0 on the rest, so its sum counts the mobile rows.

Grouped output has no fixed row order, so the examples end with `orderBy(...)`, which only sorts what's printed.

blocks.title: Count the mobile impressions per campaign
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

per_campaign = impressions.groupBy("campaign_id").agg(
    F.count("*").alias("impressions"),
    F.sum(F.when(F.col("device") == "mobile", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("mobile"),
    F.sum(F.when(F.col("device") == "desktop", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("desktop"),
)
per_campaign.orderBy("campaign_id").show()
blocks.note: Each campaign gets one row with three counts. CMP-0003 had no mobile impressions, so its mobile count is 0.

blocks.md: Why not filter first? `filter` removes rows **before** grouping, so a campaign with no matching rows has nothing left to group and disappears from the result. A conditional aggregate keeps every group, with 0 where nothing matched.

blocks.title: Filtering first loses campaigns
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

impressions.filter(F.col("device") == "tablet").groupBy("campaign_id").count().orderBy("campaign_id").show()

impressions.groupBy("campaign_id").agg(
    F.sum(F.when(F.col("device") == "tablet", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("tablet")
).orderBy("campaign_id").show()
blocks.note: Only two campaigns had a tablet impression, so the filtered version has two rows. The conditional version has all four, with 0 for the other two.

blocks.md:
Two more patterns:

- **Sum a value only where a condition holds.** `F.when(cond, F.col("revenue"))` with no `otherwise` is NULL on the other rows, and `F.sum` skips NULLs. If no row in a group matches, the sum is NULL.
- **Count matches with `F.count`.** `F.count` skips NULLs too, so `F.count(F.when(cond, True))` counts the rows where the condition is true, and gives 0 when there are none.

blocks.title: Purchase revenue and days over budget
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

conversions.groupBy("campaign_id").agg(
    F.count("*").alias("conversions"),
    F.count(F.when(F.col("conversion_type") == "purchase", True)).alias("purchases"),
    F.sum(F.when(F.col("conversion_type") == "purchase", F.col("revenue"))).alias("purchase_revenue"),
).orderBy("campaign_id").show()

budgets.groupBy("campaign_id").agg(
    F.count("*").alias("days"),
    F.count(F.when(F.col("actual_spend") > F.col("planned_spend"), True)).alias("days_over"),
).orderBy("campaign_id").show()
blocks.note: CMP-0003's only conversion is a sign-up, so it has 0 purchases and no purchase revenue. Only CMP-0001 went over its plan, on one day; spending exactly the plan isn't over.

blocks.md:
When the values you're splitting on are themselves the column names you want, use `pivot`. `groupBy("campaign_id").pivot("device")` makes one row per campaign and one column per device, and the aggregate you finish with (`.count()`, `.agg(...)`) fills each cell.

A combination with no rows gets NULL, not 0: there was nothing to count.

blocks.title: One column per device
blocks.note: Spark found three devices and made a column for each, in alphabetical order. CMP-0001 had no tablet impressions, so that cell is NULL.

blocks.md:
Without a list, Spark first has to scan the data to find the values, and the columns depend on what this particular data happens to contain: a device nobody used has no column at all. Pass the values yourself, `pivot("device", ["mobile", "desktop", "tablet"])`, to fix the columns and their order. Rows whose value isn't in the list are left out, and so are rows where it's missing.

Any aggregate works inside a pivot, not just a count.

blocks.title: Listed values and a sum
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spend = impressions.groupBy("campaign_id").pivot("device", ["mobile", "desktop", "tablet", "tv"]).agg(F.sum("cost"))
spend.orderBy("campaign_id").show()
blocks.note: The columns follow the list, including `tv`, which no impression has, so it's NULL everywhere. Each cell is the cost of that campaign's impressions on that device.

concept.prompt: A campaign has no tablet impressions. What does `F.sum(F.when(F.col("device") == "tablet", 1).otherwise(0))` give for it?
concept.why: Every row gets 0 from `otherwise`, so the sum is 0. Without `otherwise` the values would all be NULL and the sum would be NULL.

concept.prompt: Why can `df.filter(cond).groupBy("campaign_id").count()` have fewer rows than `df.groupBy("campaign_id").agg(F.count(F.when(cond, True)))`?
choices: Because a campaign with no matching rows has nothing left to group after the filter
They always have the same number of rows
concept.why: Filtering happens before grouping, so groups with no matching rows vanish. The conditional count keeps them with 0.

concept.prompt: `impressions.groupBy("campaign_id").pivot("device").count()`: what is in the cell for a campaign that had no tablet impressions?
choices: There's no tablet column at all, ever
concept.why: A pivot cell with no rows behind it is NULL. The tablet column itself exists as long as some campaign had a tablet impression, or the value is in the list you pass.

review: Put `F.when` inside an aggregate to count or sum only the rows that match: `F.sum(F.when(cond, 1).otherwise(0))`.
`F.count(F.when(cond, True))` also counts matches, because `F.count` skips NULLs.
`F.when(cond, value)` without `otherwise` is NULL elsewhere, so a sum with no matches is NULL.
Filtering before grouping drops groups with no matches; a conditional aggregate keeps them.
`groupBy(key).pivot(col)` makes one column per value; empty cells are NULL.
Pass the values to `pivot(col, [...])` to fix the columns and their order.
